cases.expectedAnswer: No. Clear space between a handrail and a wall or other surface must be at least 1.5 inches.
cases.answerText: No. For the required stair handrail, the 2022 NYC Building Code requires at least 1½ inches of clear space between the handrail and an adjacent wall or other surface; 1 inch is ½ inch short (BC §§ 1014.1, 1014.7).
cases.conclusion: No. For the required stair handrail, the 2022 NYC Building Code requires at least 1½ inches of clear space between the handrail and an adjacent wall or other surface; 1 inch is ½ inch short (BC §§ 1014.1, 1014.7).

supportingText: 1014.7 1014.7 Clearance. Clear space between a handrail and a wall or other surface shall be not less than 1 1/2 inches (38.1 mm). A handrail and a wall or other surface adjacent to the handrail shall be free of any sharp or abrasive elements.

cases.question: Under the 2022 NYC Building Code, an unobstructed exit passageway serves 49 occupants. Its capacity calculation needs no extra width. Does a 36-inch clear passageway satisfy the minimum width?
cases.expectedAnswer: Yes for minimum width. An exit passageway serving fewer than 50 occupants may be at least 36 inches wide, subject to required capacity.
cases.answerText: Yes. An exit passageway serving an occupant load of less than 50 may be at least 36 inches wide; 49 occupants is below 50, so the stated unobstructed 36-inch clear width meets that minimum (BC § 1024.2). The section also requires the passageway’s minimum width or required capacity to be unobstructed, subject to its stated encroachment exception.
cases.conclusion: Yes. An exit passageway serving an occupant load of less than 50 may be at least 36 inches wide; 49 occupants is below 50, so the stated unobstructed 36-inch clear width meets that minimum (BC § 1024.2). The section also requires the passageway’s minimum width or required capacity to be unobstructed, subject to its stated encroachment exception.

supportedPoints.heading: Minimum width for an exit passageway serving fewer than 50 occupants
supportedPoints.explanation: The required capacity is determined under Section 1005, but the default minimum width is 44 inches; the stated exception permits a minimum width of 36 inches for exit passageways serving an occupant load of less than 50. The minimum width or required capacity must be unobstructed, except for encroachments complying with Section 1005.7. At 49 occupants, the stated 36-inch width satisfies the applicable minimum.

supportingText: 1024.2 1024.2 Width. The minimum width or required capacity of exit passageways shall be unobstructed. Exception: Encroachments complying with Section 1005.7.

A lower capacity calculation does not reduce that stated minimum. The required width or capacity must be unobstructed, except for encroachments complying with BC § 1005.7 (BC § 1024.2).
cases.conclusion: **No.** At exactly 50 occupants, an exit passageway must be at least **44 inches** wide; the 36-inch exception applies only when it serves **fewer than 50**. A lower capacity calculation does not reduce that stated minimum. The required width or capacity must be unobstructed, except for encroachments complying with BC § 1005.7 (BC § 1024.2).

supportedPoints.heading: The 36-inch exception excludes exactly 50 occupants
supportedPoints.explanation: BC § 1024.2 sets a minimum width of 44 inches for exit passageways and permits 36 inches only for passageways serving an occupant load of less than 50. At exactly 50 occupants, the minimum is therefore 44 inches, regardless of whether capacity requires more. The required width or capacity must be unobstructed, except for encroachments complying with Section 1005.7.

issues.detail: The answer applies BC Table 1020.2’s 36-inch corridor-width entry to an exit passageway. The supplied source identifies Table 1020.2 as minimum corridor width (BC 1020, CORRIDORS); it does not establish that this corridor entry governs exit passageways.

For an exit passageway, BC 1024.2 sets a minimum width of 44 inches, with a 36-inch exception only when the occupant load is less than 50. At exactly 50, that exception does not apply. The answer’s conclusion that 36 inches is enough contradicts this passage.

The opening “Yes” and claim that 36 inches meets the applicable minimum imply compliance, but the supplied exit-passageway rule requires at least 44 inches at exactly 50 occupants, even if capacity does not require more.

issues.detail: The ordinary-table result of 2 is supported by the Group B rate of 1 per 100 in PC Table 403.1 and PC 403.1.1’s rule to use the total floor occupant load for Group B offices. But the separate claim that the accessibility minimum applies here is supported only by BC 1109.5.1 in its bound passage. cases.question: Under the 2022 NYC plumbing rules, ordinary indoor fixture distribution piping is at 90 psi static, and no exception applies. Is a pressure-reducing valve required, and what maximum static pressure should it reduce to?
cases.expectedAnswer: Yes. Where pressure exceeds 85 psi static, an approved reducing valve with strainer conforming to the stated standard must reduce distribution pressure to no more than 85 psi static.
cases.answerText: Yes. At 90 psi static, ordinary building water-distribution piping exceeds the 85 psi threshold, so an approved pressure-reducing valve or regulator with a strainer must reduce it to **no more than 85 psi static** (2022 NYC Plumbing Code § 604.8). The stated exception does not apply to the ordinary fixture-distribution piping in your scenario.
cases.conclusion: Yes. At 90 psi static, ordinary building water-distribution piping exceeds the 85 psi threshold, so an approved pressure-reducing valve or regulator with a strainer must reduce it to **no more than 85 psi static** (2022 NYC Plumbing Code § 604.8). The stated exception does not apply to the ordinary fixture-distribution piping in your scenario.
